title: Happy Soul, That Safe from Harm
description: Happy Soul, That Safe from Harm in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 478 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Repose of Faith”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hap-py soul, that safe from harm Rests with-in his Shep-herd's arm! Who his qui-et shall mo-lest? Who shall vi-o-late his rest?

lines: Happy soul, that safe from harm
Seek, O Lord, thy wandering sheep;
Bring me back, and lead, and keep;
Take on thee my every care;
Bear me, on thy bosom bear.
Let me know thy gracious voice;
More and more in thee rejoice;
More and more of thee receive;
Live, till all thy love I know,

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
